issues.issue: It sets a 5-year suit limitation replacing the 2-year limitation still printed in the Commercial Property Conditions (c026), so the policy carries two different limitation periods.
Defining actual cash value as repair or replacement cost "less allowance for deterioration and depreciation, including obsolescence" leaves the method and measure of that allowance entirely open.

This added definition supplies the depreciation-based figure that the Valuation condition (c121) uses, but the Coinsurance condition (c126) speaks only of "the value of Covered Property at the time of loss" and does not say whether this definition or replacement cost supplies it.

The provision applies "when coverage is provided for townhouse buildings and structures", but the Declarations describe the insured premises as apartment buildings and a storage building (c002), so its field of operation is unclear.

Limb b. says the insured's "failure to comply with any warranty or condition" will not affect the insurance if beyond its control, and the very next sentence says that if "you violate a condition of this Coverage Part, we will not pay for loss or damage at the involved location".
It supersedes the Control Of Property condition (c023-c024), whose broader rule that acts of others beyond your control "will not affect this insurance" remains printed in the policy.

Adding an exclusion for "[h]ousehold and personal property, unless owned by the Association of Townhouse Owners" to Property Not Covered has no obvious application to the apartment buildings described in the Declarations (c002).
It replaces the Mortgageholders paragraph b. (c129) with payment to an Insurance Trustee and an Association "as shown in the Townhouse Declaration", a document this policy does not contain.
It raises the per-plant sub-limit to $500 while the Outdoor Property Coverage Extension (c088) still prints $250.
It amends the Builders' Risk Coverage Form and overrides the Transfer Of Rights Of Recovery condition (c033), but no Builders' Risk form is scheduled in this policy's Declarations.

The clause first says "either may make a written request for an appraisal" and then that "an appraisal will be made only if both you and we agree, voluntarily", so the right it grants is withdrawn in the next sentence.

It replaces the Appraisal Loss Condition (c101), which makes appraisal available on one party's written demand, and does not say whether it also displaces the separate Appraisal condition in the Business Income form (c213).

It replaces the Concealment, Misrepresentation Or Fraud condition (c022), dropping that condition's requirement that a concealment be intentional and substituting non-payment for avoidance of the whole Coverage Part.
"[Y]ou" is extended here to any other person or organization qualifying as a Named Insured, while the property forms (c047, c186) confine "you" to the Named Insured shown in the Declarations.

"[T]hose sums that the insured becomes legally obligated to pay as damages" and the duty to defend "any 'suit' seeking those damages" leave the boundary between defence and indemnity to be worked out from the allegations.
The known-loss condition turns on whether an insured "knew that the 'bodily injury' or 'property damage' had occurred, in whole or in part", a partial-knowledge test the clause does not calibrate.

Two printed columns have run together, so the Contractual Liability, Liquor, Workers' Compensation and Employer's Liability exclusions are interleaved sentence by sentence and none can be read continuously.
Exclusion m. is corrupted ("'Personai would nob place, in whole or in ... afigi' or bacterla"), leaving the pollution and related exclusions unreadable as printed.

Which limb applies depends on how the insured "is designated in the Declarations", and the Commercial General Liability Declarations (c005) state "THE INSURED IS: CORPORATION" while the named insured is Boardwalk Apartments LC, a limited liability company.
"[A]cting as your real estate manager" is not defined, and the Declarations show the insured operating through Terrace Management Service.
It is expressed as "[s]ubject to 2. above", but the Each Occurrence Limit paragraph the neighbouring provisions call "5." is not reproduced anywhere in this Section III text.

The sentence is scrambled ("the Damage To Premises Pe arising out of any one 'occurrence'. Covers To You Limit is the most we will pay"), with a fragment of the Each Occurrence Limit dropped into the middle of it.
It is made "[s]ubject to 5. above", but paragraph 5 of Section III does not appear in the policy text as reproduced.
Notice is owed "as soon as practicable" of an occurrence "which may result in a claim", a double standard of timing and likelihood that the condition does not fix.
The paragraph breaks off mid-sentence ("Then, we will share ... scribed inc. below"), so the sharing rule it invokes is not stated.
